Title: Limited research
Description: Just a simple research. Web searching, AI asking and putting it all together in a dataset.

Title: Customer focus research
Description: Who is your main customer? Who will benefit from your service? How can you deliver a value?

Title: Technical focus research
Description: How to make what you wana make? What technologies would you use? How can they work together?

Title: Full scale research
Description: You throw all your resources and efforts to make your product the best fit possible. It will help in a long run... probably.

Title: Essential prototype
Description: This prototipe will just show that your idea works. It is ugly. It is buggy. But it proves the very basic concept.

Title: Service prototype
Description: This isn't a technical prototype. You have your landing page up and running, and you should do everything else by hand with every client.

Title: Technical prototype
Description: Now you know, that everything is working on the technical side. User experience? Never heard about this.

Title: Product MVP
Description: This MVP proves everything and you can ship it to selected audience. It is well designed. Well built. And it took time and effort to make it this early.

Title: Mission only
Description: Now your crew knows why are you doing what you are doing.

Title: Values and Strategy
Description: Values will help your team to make important decisions. Strategy will navigate them on which decisions they should make.

Title: Values and Mission
Description: Values will help your team to make important decisions. Mission will give them purpose to make these decisions.

Title: Values, Mission and Strategy
Description: You have done it all. Now your team knows why, how, and which decisions they should make. It invokes confidence.

Title: Internal testing
Description: Your team and friends are enough to test your product. There is no need to gather the audience.

Title: Medium focus group testing
Description: Your testing group consists of a few dozens of people both from your audience and new ones. It will help to catch criticals in your product.

Title: Real-world testing
Description: It is relatively good idea to just put your product online and acquire some users to simply use it. If you are ready to rapidly fix all appearing problems.

Title: Cascade testing with user groups
Description: Full-scale testing with several stages, each bigger. You have prepared and made it all

Title: Website building
Description: You definitely need a website. Anything else? Probaply, not.

Title: Social media setup
Description: Who needs a website when you can make it all with a proper social media account?

Title: Website and Social Media
Description: It is often easier to gather audience via social media, but they should be landed somewhere.

Title: Full marketing commitment
Description: Social media, website, community hub, press releases, and contacts with influencers. You should have it all to succeed.

Title: Single server
Description: Simple backand will be more then enough. So why bother and spend additional money on an ifrastructure? What could possibly go wrong?

Title: Cloud infrastructure
Description: Why should we bother to make our own server if we can use a cloud? It is a little bit more expensive, but definitely much more convenient.

Title: Multiple servers
Description: We know how to make it on our own with all the redundancy we need to provide a consistent service to our clients.

Title: DevOPS team with an infrastructure
Description: Infrastructure needs to be carfully planned and maintained. So we need to hire a DevOPS team to help use make this project.

Title: Self application
Description: Just prepare all the documents and send it according to instructions on a DPG website.

Title: Contact DPG office to assist
Description: We can make it with the DPG office, if they are able to help.

Title: Address SDG relevance only
Description: You have checked if your product is SDG relevant or not. If it is - so why bother? It will work anyway.

Title: DPG indicator checklist
Description: You have your checklist, so you go thugh all 9 indicators and prepare properly your application.

Title: Release marketing campaign
Description: Your team is fully focused on a marketing campaign for the release. The technical side of things is not in focus.

Title: Release event
Description: Just throw a release event to attract an audience. They will watch the stream and then they will use your product.

Title: Some release preparations
Description: You clearly have not enough time to make it all, but you can address the majore issues and prepare the campaign on a decent level.

Title: Full scale release preparations
Description: Your team is working on the release, giving attention to everything. It will take time. But since you have one, you can afford it.

Title: Essential support only
Description: We don't have enough resources for the full scale support, so we will do only bare essentials.

Title: Phone and email customer support
Description: We will conduct a customer support via both phone and email.

Title: Support with LiveOPS
Description: We will not only make a support up and running, but also establish regular events and activities for our clients (LiveOPS).

Title: Outsourced support
Description: We no need our team to make a customer support. Let's hire an outsource company to make it for us!

Title: Listening Sessions
Description: Meet speakers and librarians to learn which local expressions need context. Start with a small collection and record its limits.

Title: Community Priorities
Description: Ask regional groups which stories they want preserved. Focus on useful entries rather than technical experiments.

Title: Recording Research
Description: Test microphones and searchable transcripts with volunteers. Learn how to store speech without losing its original sound.

Title: Regional Field Study
Description: Combine community interviews with recording trials across several regions. Gather broader evidence before choosing the archive's scope.

Title: Audio Card Demo
Description: Build a simple page with one recording and its meaning. Test the core idea before adding a large collection.

Title: Librarian-Led Trial
Description: Let a librarian guide visitors through sample recordings by hand. Observe what people ask before automating the service.

Title: Transcript Search Demo
Description: Prototype audio storage and search for Kazakh text. Test the pipeline first; a polished browsing experience comes later.

Title: Working Archive Pilot
Description: Build a small working archive with audio playback and reviewed transcripts. Give selected speakers a complete experience to test.

Title: Shared Purpose
Description: Agree that Qazaq Heritage preserves regional voices without ranking them. Keep team planning light for now.

Title: Editorial Playbook
Description: Define review roles and a collection strategy. Help volunteers make consistent decisions about context and attribution.

Title: Speaker Partnership
Description: Build the team around a shared mission and contributor values. Include regional reviewers in everyday editorial decisions.

Title: Community Charter
Description: Agree on purpose, review roles and a long-term plan with community representatives. Prepare a clear process for resolving disagreements.

Title: Team Listening Test
Description: Ask staff and friends to try the archive. This is quick, but misses many regional voices and listening habits.

Title: Regional Listener Panel
Description: Invite speakers and learners to test a small set of entries. Use their feedback to refine meanings and context.

Title: Public Archive Trial
Description: Open a limited collection for real visitors. Learn how people discover recordings while responding to problems as they appear.

Title: Multi-Region Pilot
Description: Test the archive with several groups in stages. Compare feedback before expanding the collection to a wider audience.

Title: Archive Information Site
Description: Explain the collection's purpose and how recordings are reviewed. Give partners a reliable place to understand the project.

Title: Community Audio Posts
Description: Share approved short excerpts through community channels. Focus on reaching listeners before building a full campaign.

Title: Library Outreach Kit
Description: Combine an archive website with sample posts for local libraries. Help partners introduce the collection to their audiences.

Title: Regional Launch Network
Description: Prepare library contacts, community demonstrations and public information pages. Invest in a broad outreach effort.

Title: Small Archive Server
Description: Run the initial collection on one server. Keep costs low, but accept limited resilience if it fails.

Title: Managed Audio Hosting
Description: Use managed hosting for recordings and transcripts. Reduce routine maintenance while taking on a higher service bill.

Title: Independent Archive Mirrors
Description: Run your own archive servers in more than one location. Improve availability, but leave extra maintenance to the team.

Title: Archive Operations Team
Description: Plan storage, deployment and recovery with dedicated operations staff. Build room to grow at a substantial cost.

Title: Prepare DPG Evidence
Description: Document the code license, public benefit and content permissions. Assemble the application with your own team.

Title: Seek Application Guidance
Description: Ask for guidance on the DPG application process. Use the discussion to coordinate the team's evidence gathering.

Title: Heritage Statement Only
Description: Write only about the cultural mission. Without checking other requirements, the application may lack essential evidence.

Title: Review Every Indicator
Description: Check the archive against the DPG indicators and assemble supporting evidence. Treat public benefit as a starting point, not the whole application.

Title: Library Launch Campaign
Description: Promote the archive through libraries and cultural groups. Focus on visibility rather than technical release work.

Title: Live Listening Event
Description: Host a streamed listening session with approved excerpts. Attract attention, but divert staff from other release tasks.

Title: Focused Launch Checks
Description: Check key pages and prepare a modest announcement. Prioritize the essentials within a short release window.

Title: Coordinated Archive Release
Description: Rehearse the release, brief partners and check the service. A wider preparation effort needs more time and money.

Title: Essential Archive Care
Description: Keep playback working and fix urgent errors. Limit support commitments to what the current team can sustain.

Title: Speaker Help Desk
Description: Offer phone and email support for contributors and listeners. Maintain a personal service with extra workload for staff.

Title: Community Listening Programme
Description: Run regular listening sessions alongside support. Build lasting participation, but commit staff to ongoing activities.

Title: Contracted Support Desk
Description: Pay an external team to handle routine questions using your review guide. Free internal capacity at a higher upfront cost.
